Studying 6-10 hours a day is not normal!😭🤯 It means you could be much more efficient! More hours don't necessarily mean doing better, and in the long run, you get tired, take more time, and lose motivation. I went from studying 6-8 hours a day to covering the same amount of material in just one hour. I also finally started remembering what I studied long-term and fell in love with studying again, rediscovering my motivation. ❌And no, it wasn't thanks to Feynman, Blurting or Pomodoro. Here's how you can do it: 🕐TimeLimits: Your brain takes all the time available to complete a task. So if we give ourselves 2 hours to study, we'll unconsciously take 2 hours.Set study limits that are less time than what you usually study, maybe 1 hour less to start with. You'll notice that you'll finish the same amount of work in the set time, but you'll stay much more focused. 🔥Productivity Peak Hours: Identify the times during the day when you're most productive and use 1-2 hours of that time to study with maximum focus.When we're mentally more energized, our brains work faster and we remember better. 🧠Mind maps: You've probably heard of them, but if you're not using them yet, it's probably because you've never tried Tony Buzan's method. I used to think they were only for reviewing, but since l learned how to make them the right way, I use them to take notes in class. I can memorize long-term information, and the time I spend studying has dropped drastically. Mind maps are the fastest and most effective way to take notes. Studies show that by just doing a mind map, you remember up to 60% of the information.
